summary: ReactiveUI ecosystem infrastructure for DI, service location, logging, and composition-root registration.
recommendedPatterns: Use Splat registration at the composition root.
Prefer generic registration and resolution APIs.
Prefer constructor injection in application code.
avoidPatterns: Do not spread global service-location calls through feature logic.
Do not assume shared mutable global resolver state is safe for libraries or tests.
setupSteps: Add Splat when DI or resolver integration is needed.
Keep library code independent from global resolver mutation where possible.
commonPitfalls: Leaking global resolver state between tests.
Using service locator instead of explicit dependencies in business logic.

features: Generic-first dependency resolution and service location
Transient, constant, lazy-singleton, contract, and multi-registration services
DI adapters for Autofac, DryIoc, Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection, Ninject, Prism, and SimpleInjector
Cross-platform colours, geometry, bitmap loading, conversion, saving, and SkiaSharp integration
functions: GetService<T>, GetServices<T>, Register<T>, RegisterConstant<T>, and RegisterLazySingleton<T>
AppBuilder, IModule.Configure, UsingModule, WithCustomRegistration, UseCurrentSplatLocator, and Build
options: Global generic-first resolver for a controlled application-wide container and the hottest resolution path
Instance generic-first resolver for libraries, independent resolver instances, and test isolation
Generic APIs for compile-time-known types or Type-based APIs for legacy adapters and runtime discovery
Transient, eager constant, lazy singleton, named-contract, or multiple-implementation registration
Direct Splat resolver or one supported external-container adapter
Composable AppBuilder/IModule startup or direct composition-root registration
Null, console, or debug logging and Log4Net, Microsoft.Extensions.Logging, NLog, or Serilog adapters
Core packages only, drawing/SkiaSharp packages, and optional APM integrations
packageSelection: Use Splat for the complete default surface, or select Splat.Core, Splat.Builder, Splat.Logging, and Splat.Drawing when a narrower library dependency is appropriate.
Add exactly one DI adapter when the composition root uses Autofac, DryIoc, Microsoft.Extensions.DependencyInjection, Ninject, Prism, or SimpleInjector.
Add Splat.Microsoft.Extensions.Logging, Splat.Log4Net, Splat.NLog, or Splat.Serilog only for the selected logging backend.
Add Splat.Drawing and optionally Splat.SkiaSharp only for shared colour, geometry, bitmap, or SkiaSharp integration requirements.
Add Splat.ApplicationInsights, Splat.ApplicationInsightsV3, Splat.Exceptionless, or Splat.Raygun only when that monitoring backend is intentionally configured.
Add Splat.DependencyInjection.SourceGenerator as a PrivateAssets=all analyzer alongside Splat for static registration graphs; it is maintained in a separate repository.
sourceGeneratorGuidance: Use Splat.DependencyInjection.SourceGenerator as the primary choice for compile-time-known registration graphs, constructor/property injection, and AOT-friendly composition.
Retain Splat manual or container-specific registration for dynamic discovery, plugins, unsupported open generics, and other runtime-selected services.
Prefer generic registration and resolution APIs whenever the service type is known at compile time; reserve Type-based APIs for compatibility and runtime-loaded types.
compatibilityNotes: The Splat package family supports desktop, mobile, Avalonia, MAUI, WinUI, WPF, WinForms, shared-library, and multi-targeted application scenarios documented upstream.
GenericFirst resolvers are AOT-compatible; ModernDependencyResolver remains available for backward compatibility but is not the recommendation for new code.
Global resolver registrations are process-wide and require teardown discipline; instance resolver registrations provide isolation for tests and libraries.
Configure ReactiveUI and the selected external-container integration before the container is finalized so framework registrations and logging are composed correctly.
Splat.DependencyInjection.SourceGenerator is a companion package and repository, not functionality embedded into the Splat runtime packages.
migrationGuidance: Move ModernDependencyResolver usage to a GenericFirst resolver and migrate hot-path Type-based calls to generic APIs incrementally.
Move scattered Locator or AppLocator mutation into one application composition root, then replace feature-level service location with constructor injection.
Use InstanceGenericFirstDependencyResolver for libraries and tests that must avoid shared global registrations.
Move startup registrations into explicit IModule implementations and build them once with AppBuilder; use HasRegistration for reusable idempotent modules.
Migrate handwritten static registration factories to Splat.DependencyInjection.SourceGenerator when the graph is statically analyzable, retaining manual adapters for runtime-discovered services.
